overall: Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by reorganizing at its January 2 inauguration meeting without listing it on the notice; the other allegations, including the request to void later actions, were not violations or were outside jurisdiction.

allegations.summary: Committee nominated and voted on a Chair and Vice Chair at its January 2 inauguration meeting, a topic not listed on the posted notice.
allegations.key_passage: Where the Committee failed to include such a topic on its January 2 meeting notice, we find that the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Same January 2 complaint, framed as a Vice Chair nomination and vote made without reorganization being listed on the notice.
allegations.key_passage: Discussion concerning the leadership of the Committee is a matter of public business that should be discussed during an open meeting and listed as a topic on the notice.

allegations.summary: Challenge that all actions taken while the Chair presided (January 4, 9, 16, 23 meetings) are void because the Chair allegedly posted meetings improperly.
allegations.key_passage: As such, we find that the Committee did not violate the Open Meeting Law when it met on those dates and took actions and made decisions.

allegations.summary: Claim that the Chair cannot legally run Committee meetings because she was not validly elected Chair.
allegations.key_passage: Finally, the Open Meeting Law does not specifically require that a public body appoint a member as chair nor does the law mandate that only a specific public body member, such as the chair, has authority to “run” a meeting.

allegations.summary: Claim that the Chair illegally assumed the title at the January 2 meeting and so lacks authority to act for the Committee.
allegations.key_passage: whether Ms. Nixon “illegally assumed the title of” Chair during that meeting is a matter outside the jurisdiction of this office.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law's requirements, ordered for the Committee.
remedy_passage: We order the Committee’s immediate and future compliance with the law’s requirements
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
